newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas steady to lower amid cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas steady to lower amid cooler weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices on average were little changed Monday amid cooler-than-normal weather throughout the Northeast and Midwest, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast gas prices at the Henry Hub, La., began lower at $2.05-2.09 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) but gradually rose to match levels seen on Friday at $2.07-2.11.
Similarly in south Texas, where cooler air lurked nearby, prices slipped two cents to about $2 per mmBtu.
Temperatures throughout the southern plains and Texas are expected to dip to five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below normal later this week.
At the New York city-gate, prices eased a few cents to about $2.32-2.40 as temperatures in the region lagged only a few degrees below normal.
The coldest days are expected on Thursday and Friday when temperatures are forecast to fall to about five to seven degrees F below normal.
Meanwhile, Appalachian prices slipped about five cents to $2.27-2.29 on Columbia and $2.30-2.33 on CNG.

In the Midcontinent, prices on average were one cent lower in the low-$1.90s, though some late deals were reported done at $1.95 and $1.96. Cooler forecasts for this week helped to prevent prices from falling by a sharper amount, traders said.
Demarcation prices remained in the low-to-mid $1.90s, while Chicago city-gate prices were quoted about seven cents lower at $2.09-2.13. At Detroit city-gate, deals were reported done at $2.23-2.26.
Early indications for May 1 delivery on the most of the Midcontinent pipes centered in the mid-$1.90s, market sources said, showing a jump of about 20 cents from April indices.
Further west, Permian basin prices for Tuesday delivery eased one cent to the high-$1.80s, while Waha values were quoted at $1.92-1.95.

Similarly at the southern California border, prices lost one cent to about $2.04-2.06. Significantly cooler weather is forecast to arrive to the Southwest Thursday and Friday, Weather Services Corp said.
